rot.deletang.curiosidades.deletang: Daniel Delétang published the complete method in 1923, in the French magazine La Stratégie; some of its ideas date back to 1780. It is not the shortest way to mate, but it is simple to remember.
rot.deletang.ideia.ex1.e1: Attack: the black king is near a1, but with a light-squared bishop the mating net only works in a light corner. The nearest one is h1.
rot.deletang.ideia.ex1.e2: The bishop on g6 watches the diagonal from b1 to h7: with the first rank and the h-file, it closes Delétang's big triangle. The black king can only cross sideways, as from d2 to c3, and your king on b2 closes that passage.
rot.deletang.ideia.ex1.e3: The plan: push the black king towards h1 and shrink the triangle, moving the bishop to smaller diagonals parallel to this one, such as d1 to h5.
rot.deletang.ideia.ex1.l1: The bishop slides to c2 without leaving the diagonal: the triangle is the same, and now d1 is watched too.
rot.deletang.ideia.ex1.l2: With no square on the d-file, the black king goes up to e3, away from the edge. The knight on e6 watches d4, the sideways passage across the diagonal.
rot.deletang.ideia.ex1.l3: Your king goes to c1, next to the bishop, and takes d2 away from the black king. Your king's route is up the d-file.
rot.deletang.ideia.ex1.l4: The black king returns to e2 and watches d1 and d2: your king cannot advance.
rot.deletang.ideia.ex1.l5: Waiting move: the bishop goes back to g6, on the same diagonal. The triangle does not change, but now the black king has to leave e2.
rot.deletang.ideia.ex1.l6: The black king goes up to e3 again, away from the edge, and leaves d1 free for your king; d2 is still watched by it.
rot.deletang.ideia.ex1.l7: Your king steps into d1 and watches e1 and e2. The black king has only f2 and f3.
rot.deletang.ideia.ex1.l8: The black king goes to f2, right next to e1: your king can only leave d1 for a square that still watches e1.
rot.deletang.ideia.ex1.l9: Your king goes up to d2 and watches e1, e2 and e3.
rot.deletang.ideia.ex1.l10: The black king goes up to f3 looking for the centre, but e4 is watched by the bishop.
rot.deletang.ideia.ex1.l11: Your king goes to d3 and watches e2, e3 and e4. The black king is stuck to the right of the e-file.
rot.deletang.ideia.ex1.l12: The black king returns to f2 and eyes e1 and d1: with your king on d3, no white piece watches d1.
rot.deletang.ideia.ex1.l13: The bishop switches to the diagonal from d1 to h5 and closes d1. The switch is safe: your king on d3 closes e3, and the knight closes f4 and g5. The triangle has shrunk: d1, h1 and h5.
rot.deletang.ideia.ex2.e1: Attack: another position. The bishop on h5 already closes the middle triangle, from d1 to h5, and the black king is near h1. What remains is the small triangle, from f1 to h3, and the mating net.
rot.deletang.ideia.ex2.l1: The bishop goes to e2, on the same diagonal, and watches f1 and f3. The black king is left with h1, h2, h3 and g1.
rot.deletang.ideia.ex2.l2: The black king goes up to h3 and eyes h4, the way out along the h-file.
rot.deletang.ideia.ex2.l3: Your king goes to g5 and closes g4 and h4.
rot.deletang.ideia.ex2.l4: With no way up, the black king returns to g2, where it has more squares.
rot.deletang.ideia.ex2.l5: Your king comes down to g4 and takes h3 and g3 away from the black king.
rot.deletang.ideia.ex2.l6: The black king goes to h2, from where it can still return to g2.
rot.deletang.ideia.ex2.l7: The bishop switches to the diagonal from f1 to h3 and closes g2: this is the small triangle, f1, h1 and h3.
rot.deletang.ideia.ex2.l8: The black king goes to g1 and attacks the bishop on f1.
rot.deletang.ideia.ex2.l9: The bishop escapes to h3, on the same diagonal: g2 and f1 are still watched.
rot.deletang.ideia.ex2.l10: The black king goes to h1, away from your king.
rot.deletang.ideia.ex2.l11: Your king goes to g3 and takes away h2 and g2. The black king has only g1.
rot.deletang.ideia.ex2.l12: Forced move: the black king goes to g1.
rot.deletang.ideia.ex2.l13: The knight goes to d2, on its way to f3, the mating square.
rot.deletang.ideia.ex2.l14: Forced move: the black king returns to h1.
rot.deletang.ideia.ex2.l15: Check on g2: the bishop, protected by your king, takes away h1 and pushes the black king to g1.
rot.deletang.ideia.ex2.l16: Forced move: the black king goes to g1.
rot.deletang.ideia.ex2.l17: Checkmate: the knight on f3 gives check, the bishop watches f1 and h1, and your king protects the bishop and watches f2 and h2.
rot.deletang.demos.fuga.1: Attack demonstration: what if the bishop leaves the diagonal from b1 to h7 instead of waiting on it?
rot.deletang.demos.fuga.2: The bishop goes to a4 and abandons the diagonal: d3 is free.
rot.deletang.demos.fuga.3: The black king crosses through d3 and leaves the triangle.
rot.deletang.demos.fuga.4: The bishop goes to c6 and watches d5 and e4, but the black king is already out.
rot.deletang.demos.fuga.5: The black king goes to c3, heading for a1: everything starts again, eight moves further from mate.
rot.deletang.demos.afogar.1: Attack demonstration: the black king is on h1, in the small triangle. If the knight goes to f3 right now, the black king is stalemated.
rot.deletang.demos.afogar.2: Your king goes to f2 and takes away g1; h2 is left free on purpose, so the black king has a move.
rot.deletang.demos.afogar.3: Forced move: the black king goes to h2.
rot.deletang.demos.afogar.4: Now the knight reaches f3 with check.
rot.deletang.demos.afogar.5: Forced move: the black king returns to h1.
rot.deletang.demos.afogar.6: Checkmate: the bishop on g2, protected by your king, gives check, and the knight watches g1 and h2.
rot.deletang.pratica.medio.p: Attack: play White and deliver mate. Go from the middle triangle to the small one; your king and the knight close the sideways passages.
rot.deletang.pratica.medio.fim: Checkmate: from the middle triangle to the small one, up to the final net.
rot.deletang.pratica.grande.p: Attack: play White and deliver mate. Start with the big triangle and shrink it one at a time.
rot.deletang.pratica.grande.fim: End of the chapter: big, middle and small triangle, one at a time, up to the mating net.
rot.deletang.pratica.fins.afogado: Stalemate: the black king had no move and was not in check. Before closing the last square, check that the move gives check.
rot.deletang.pratica.fins.repeticao: The position was repeated three times: draw. Shrink the triangle at each step, without going back.
rot.deletang.pratica.fins.limite: The move limit ran out before mate. Do not let the black king leave the triangle: switch diagonals only with the passages closed by your king and the knight.
rot.deletang.pratica.fins.insuficiente: A piece was captured, and the material is not enough for mate. Keep the bishop and the knight protected.
